Symbols and terms used in this deck

TermMeaningTermMeaning
Stationa stop on the outside-operator round (13 in all)Local gaugePG, TG, LG, FG: read only in the field, not on the DCS
HV-9xxhand valve, a field-only item; 9xx is the P&ID series for theseNOnormally open
CSOcar-sealed open: a seal shows it has not been movedLClocked closed: opening needs a key and a permit

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • The 3-D plant uses the Layout tab's coordinates; every reading is live.
  • The round starts at the heater because it is upwind, and ends at the desalters.
  • Most gauges are read at grade; plan the climbs so each level is visited once.

Part 2

What does a hand valve do to the live plant?

Part 2 · the plan

Fourteen valves, one map in the model

  1. The fourteen valvesnormal position and effect when moved
  2. Instrument air losthow fast valves go to their fail position
  3. A bypass openedhow much gas goes to the flare

Step 1 · interactive · hand valves

What happens if this valve is moved?

Step 2 · interactive · HV-986 closed

How long until the valves fail?

header bleed$a(t) = e^{-t/\tau}$,   $\tau = 15$ s; fail when $a < 0.4$

Step 3 · interactive · HV-985 opened

How much gas leaves through the bypass?

model$F = 800\sqrt{P_{drum}/13.8}$   Nm³/h

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • A closed suction valve trips a running pump in about 4 s; a closed discharge valve in about 8 s.
  • With HV-986 closed the air header falls below 0.4 after 13.7 s and the V-4 valves fail.
  • HV-985 opened sends about 800 Nm³/h to the flare; the drum pressure then falls.

Part 3

How is a round written down and checked?

Part 3 · the plan

Readings, states and names

  1. The rounds sheethow close a reading must be
  2. Identificationname the equipment from its shape

Step 1 · interactive · rounds sheet

How close must a reading be?

accepted$|x - x_{plant}| \le \max(a,\ f\,|x_{plant}|)$

Step 2 · interactive · identification

How many items must you name right?

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • The 28-row sheet is checked against the plant at that moment, not against design.
  • Numbers pass within a few per cent; pumps and valves must match exactly.
  • Identification passes at 90 %: 22 of the 24 items.

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the round in order and read every local gauge yourself.

2

Check every hand valve against its normal position: NO, CSO or LC.

3

Never move a car-sealed or locked valve on a round.

4

Write what you see, then compare it with the DCS.
